problem: VLMs keep no persistent memory or explicit spatial representation of a scene, so all sampled frames must be re-processed for every query and cost scales as O(queries x frames). Existing persistent representations either need 3D reconstruction/depth (scene graphs) or lack object-level semantics (topological graphs).
motivation: Robots that traverse an environment once must later answer questions and find goals long after observation, with low latency and explainable reasoning. Building a queryable object-level graph once from monocular video could decouple query latency from video length.
key_idea: Build a persistent spatiotemporal knowledge graph from monocular egocentric video, using VLM chunk detection and LLM-based object association across chunks, then answer queries by GraphRAG subgraph retrieval fused with SigLIP2 object-level visual grounding.
insight: Persistent identity matters: removing cross-chunk association (CwGR) drops answer accuracy from 50.0 to 37.2. Graph and visual encoder are complementary: GER-G beats SigLIP2-G alone by +6.7 Retr.@1 and beats graph-only GR (65.8 vs 53.2), while only the graph gives answers. The full graph as context gives the best answer accuracy (58.1) but worse localization than GER-G, and chunk size b=8 is a sweet spot (b=5 fragments, b=15 crowds).
method: Chunked VLM detection: video split into chunks of b=8 frames; Gemini 2.5 Flash with multi-image prompts outputs per-chunk object descriptors (id, attributes, per-frame bboxes) and pairwise relations from 20 spatial predicates as a chunk graph.

STOA (Spatiotemporal Object Association): an LLM receives the accumulated graph and the new chunk graph and decides per object whether it matches an existing ID or is new, using type, attributes and relational context on text (prompt rule: prefer reuse when in doubt), so identity survives visual gaps.
Graph database storage: the final graph is persistent and queried without re-processing raw video.

GraphRAG retrieval (GR): query term extraction plus LLM query rewriting to graph vocabulary; lexical scoring of objects aggregated per frame; top-m frames' full local subgraphs are serialized to an LLM that produces the answer and ranked frames.
Graph-Enhanced Retrieval (GER): SigLIP2 (Large or Giant) embeddings of object bbox crops; query text embedding cosine search; union with graph-retrieved candidates into one subgraph (GER-L / GER-G).

WalkieKnowledge benchmark: 193 manually annotated questions on 8 EgoWalk egocentric trajectories, 4 question types, frame-level GT, evaluated with Retrieval Acc/Recall/Precision/MRR@k and answer accuracy.
Real-robot pipeline: each node keeps source frame and SLAM pose; the top-1 retrieved frame's pose is sent to the ROS navigation stack as goal.

setting.backbone: Gemini 2.5 Flash (frozen; KG construction and reasoning) + SigLIP2 L/G (frozen) for GER; Qwen3.5-Plus as ablation backbone
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB video (no depth, no 3D reconstruction); SLAM poses only in real-robot deployment
setting.action_space: none for QA; retrieved goal frame and pose sent to a classical ROS navigation stack in the real robot
setting.privileged: none (for WalkieKnowledge, frames containing answers were added to decimated set if none were sampled)

numbers.extra: EM-EQA, 32 sampled frames per episode; graph built once

numbers.eval_set_note: descriptive (binary and text) queries only; positional queries excluded

numbers.evidence: Table overall performance on WalkieKnowledge, GER-G column

numbers.eval_set_note: real office environments, queries across four WalkieKnowledge categories
numbers.extra: real differential-drive robot with SLAM Toolbox + ROS nav; same SR as Gemini 2.5 Pro

numbers_note: Which VL-KnG variant/backbone was used in the robot experiment is not stated explicitly. OpenEQA split is not named in the paper (assigned 'val'). NaVQA and WalkieKnowledge splits are not named either.
results: On WalkieKnowledge, GER-G reaches 65.8% Retr.@1 and 0.735 MRR@5, beating RoboHop (34.7), Qwen2.5-VL-72B (48.2) and WMNav (52.9), with 0.8 s vs ~108 s per query for WMNav. It approaches Gemini 2.5 Pro (68.9) and Qwen3.5+ (66.3) at ~30x lower latency. On NaVQA GER-G gets 0.662 versus DAAAM 0.672 and ReMEmbR-8B 0.607; on OpenEQA GER-L gets 55.2 versus GPT-4V 49.6, but far below Gemini 3 Flash (76.8).
limitations: Fine-grained spatial reasoning is weak because positions are only frame-level with no 3D geometry; spatial-relation questions remain hardest.
Graph quality is bounded by the VLM's detection ability, and STOA assumes mostly static scenes.
